title: Impact of Elite High School Admission on SAT Scores

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD). This is appropriate because admission is determined by a test score cutoff, creating a quasi-random assignment around the threshold. The key assumption is that students just above and below the cutoff are similar in all unobserved characteristics except for treatment status. The running variable (admission test score) should be continuous around the cutoff, and there should be no precise manipulation of the assignment variable.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(rddensity)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s90_data.csv")

# Display basic summary
print("Data Summary:")
print(summary(data))

# Determine the cutoff (threshold where treatment changes)
cutoff <- min(data$running_var[data$treated == 1])
print(paste("Cutoff threshold:", cutoff))

# Center the running variable around the cutoff
data$running_var_centered <- data$running_var - cutoff

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                       x = data$running_var_centered, 
                       c = 0,
                       kernel = "triangular",
                       p = 1)

# Print main results
print("=== MAIN RDD RESULTS ===")
print(paste("RDD Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4)))
print(paste("Standard Error:", round(rdd_result$se[1], 4)))
print(paste("P-value:", round(rdd_result$pv[1], 4)))
print(paste("95% Confidence Interval: [", 
            round(rdd_result$ci[1,1], 4), ",", 
            round(rdd_result$ci[1,2], 4), "]"))

# Robustness checks
print("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===")

# 1. Different bandwidth
rdd_robust1 <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                        x = data$running_var_centered, 
                        c = 0,
                        h = rdd_result$bws[1,1] * 0.8)
print(paste("RDD with 80% bandwidth:", round(rdd_robust1$coef[1], 4)))

# 2. Quadratic specification
rdd_robust2 <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                        x = data$running_var_centered, 
                        c = 0,
                        p = 2)
print(paste("RDD with quadratic fit:", round(rdd_robust2$coef[1], 4)))

# 3. Test for manipulation (density test)
density_test <- rddensity(data$running_var_centered, c = 0)
print(paste("Manipulation test p-value:", round(density_test$test$p_jk, 4)))

# 4. Balance test on pre-treatment characteristic (using running_var as proxy)
# Test if there's a discontinuity in the running variable itself (should be smooth)
balance_test <- rdrobust(y = abs(data$running_var_centered), 
                        x = data$running_var_centered, 
                        c = 0)
print(paste("Balance test coefficient:", round(balance_test$coef[1], 4)))
print(paste("Balance test p-value:", round(balance_test$pv[1], 4)))

# Create visualization
plot_data <- data[order(data$running_var_centered), ]
plot_data$fitted_left <- NA
plot_data$fitted_right <- NA

# Fit local polynomials for visualization
left_data <- plot_data[plot_data$running_var_centered < 0, ]
right_data <- plot_data[plot_data$running_var_centered >= 0, ]

if(nrow(left_data) > 0) {
  left_fit <- loess(y ~ running_var_centered, data = left_data, span = 0.75)
  plot_data$fitted_left[plot_data$running_var_centered < 0] <- predict(left_fit)
}

if(nrow(right_data) > 0) {
  right_fit <- loess(y ~ running_var_centered, data = right_data, span = 0.75)
  plot_data$fitted_right[plot_data$running_var_centered >= 0] <- predict(right_fit)
}

# Print final summary
print("\n=== SUMMARY ===")
print(paste("The estimated effect of elite high school admission on SAT scores is:", 
            round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4)))
if(rdd_result$pv[1] < 0.05) {
  print("This effect is statistically significant at the 5% level.")
} else {
  print("This effect is not statistically significant at the 5% level.")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive treatment effect of approximately 0.1-0.3 standard deviations in SAT scores. Elite high schools typically provide better resources, more rigorous curriculum, and enhanced college preparation, which should translate to higher SAT performance. The effect should be statistically significant given that elite institutions are designed to improve academic outcomes. The magnitude reflects that while institutional quality matters, individual ability (already captured in the admission test) remains the primary determinant of SAT performance.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare SAT scores of students just above and below the admission cutoff.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Admission to the elite high school slightly decreases SAT scores.
